The `react-result-*.json` files record actual `getBoundingClientRect` geometry and computed styles from the existing React `src/views/ResultWindow/ResultWindow.tsx` rendered in WKWebView. They are independent of `ResultUi`.

Run Vite at `127.0.0.1:5194`, then `cargo run -p snaplingo --example result_reference_snapshot`. The isolated React fixture is `crates/snaplingo-app/tests/native_ui/result_reference.tsx`; it injects only state and runtime ports. It does not start Tauri or alter installed settings. Screenshots and measurements go to `target/shared-result/reference`.

The regression compares Native translation and OCR panel, textarea, provider cards, and action buttons within 0.5 logical DIP. Studio dark and Paper at 175% also check panel geometry and palette; CSS zoom snaps borders to WebKit device pixels, so the zoomed fixture permits up to 2 logical DIP of accumulated edge rounding. OCR image scenes additionally compare the contained image, upload button, editable text, fragment heading and buttons, and footer in Native, Studio dark, and Paper at 175%. A short viewport checks scrolling and clip boundaries. Actual clicks in the React reference copy `support@example.com` and `2026-11-09 14:30`; shared pointer tests assert the same values and targets. The independent geometry suite has four passing cases, and current Rust renders are generated with `cargo run -p snaplingo-render --example result_snapshot -- target/shared-result`.
